title: Ramayana vs Adipurush: How Ranbir Kapoor and Yash's film fixes the biggest mistakes of Prabhas' mythological epic
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ever since the rollout of the trailer of Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana today, comparing it to Om Raut’s Adipurush has been inevitable. While the two movies may be based on the same epic, which is among the most respected mythological epics of India, everything else differs from then onwards. Right from how Lord Ram and Ravana have been projected to the visual effects, music and more, the trailers look entirely different.

Adding to this, Ramayana trailer vs Adipurush: 5 major differences between Ranbir Kapoor's epic and Prabhas' movie. Adipurush, when it premiered in 2023, received major backlash because of its visual effects and the way its characters were designed. Ramayana, on the other hand, has seemed to consider these aspects very well. When the character of Lord Rama was introduced in April 2026 with a teaser trailer, it too suffered the same problem and there were questions raised about whether Ranbir will be able to portray this role well. Although the trailer, which launched during Brahma Muhurta at 4:15 received some criticism, it has still felt like a more emotionally grounded and respectful retelling. Here's how both these versions compare with each other.

Meanwhile, The most distinctive feature in terms of these trailers is the presentation of Lord Rama. While in Adipurush, Prabhas (Raghava) is portrayed as a warrior, marching ahead with his army into the war. The trailer is quite dynamic and full of loud battle cries and strong dialogues. This character is motivated by his anger towards evil as he motivates his army to “crush the chest of ego” and raise the flag of victory.

Notably, On the contrary, Ramayana provides an introduction to Ranbir Kapoor (Rama), who is rather emotional and gentle character even when he is in exile and headed for war. His words, “If my life must be the price for prosperity… I would give it gladly,” and “As a son, it is my duty to honour my father's word,” make it clear that he is a compassionate, sacrificing and righteous leader. Moreover, it seems that the movie presents the traditional image of Maryada Purushottam, but not an action hero. The title means supreme person who is following his morality and behaves accordingly to the code of honour.

As per the latest buzz, The two trailers also present completely different versions of Ravana. Saif Ali Khan (Lankesh) in Adipurush sparked debate soon after the trailer arrived. His buzzcut, dark blue eyes and fantasy-inspired styling reminded many viewers of a modern comic-book villain, someone you would see in Game of Thrones maybe or Vikings, rather than the legendary king of Lanka. The dark colour palette, Gothic architecture and giant CGI bats further pushed the character away from familiar depictions from mythology.

In further updates, Yash (Ravana) in Ramayana goes in the opposite direction. The trailer gives him a royal appearance with elaborate golden armour, traditional styling and a commanding presence. Rama's dialogue, “If Ravana is the ruler of all three realms… then all three worlds shall witness his death,” adds weight to the character, making him look powerful, intelligent and dangerous without moving too far away from the epic's roots.

On top of that, Visual effects were among the biggest talking points around Adipurush, with many viewers saying the movie looked more like a video game than a historical epic. Much of the world felt overly dependent on CGI, making several sequences appear artificial.

Ramayana's trailer creates a different impression. From Ayodhya and the Swayamvar arena to the forests and battlefields, the locations feel more detailed and lived-in. Instead of relying entirely on digital backgrounds, the movie appears to combine large physical sets with visual effects. Even creatures like Jatayu look more realistic, while the large crowd scenes have greater depth and scale.

title: Mamta Kulkarni reacts to Mahira Sharma's Ranaji 2.0, says the original is 'etched in people's minds'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

More than three decades after Karan Arjun gave Bollywood the iconic Mujhko Ranaji Maaf Karna, the song has returned in a new avatar. Titled Ranaji 2.0, the recreated version stars Mahira Sharma and is choreographed by Remo D'Souza.

Adding to this, In conversation with Variety India, she shared, "She has done a good job. The point is that you're watching a song that was originally in ghagra choli and Indian dance moves, now made in a western format and in a western outfit. So, it stands out. But the earlier song is etched in people's minds, so it immediately comes to your mind."

Meanwhile, Mamta also reflected on filming the original number, recalling that choreographer Chinni Prakash had planned two to three days of rehearsals, but she picked up the steps on the very first day. However, she was surprised when the choreography was changed on the day of the shoot.
Notably, "I asked him why he had changed the steps. I wondered what the point of the rehearsals was, but Chinni Prakash masterji was very good, and we wrapped up the song on time," she recalled.
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Mahira Sharma (@mahirasharma)

In further updates, She also credited director Rakesh Roshan for pulling off the ambitious movie with such a large ensemble cast and memorable music. "Jai Maa Kaali was difficult to shoot because there were many dancers. I give credit to Rakeshji for completing such a complicated movie with so many artists. Karan Arjun became a superhit. Whether it was Jai Maa Kaali, Bhangda Paa Le or Ek Munda Meri Umr Da, people loved all the songs," she shared.

On top of that, The star also opened up that she has been receiving acting offers and is open to returning to films if she finds a script that excites her. However, she admitted that her outlook has changed over the years and she is now more conscious about the projects she takes up.

"I've been receiving acting offers. If I get a script I'm truly excited about, I'm ready to take it on. Of course, I won't be able to do a song like Mujhko Ranaji Maaf Karna today with these lyrics. I'm spiritually conscious and awakened now," she shared.

title: Kirti Kulhari falls victim to cyber fraud, loses Rs 2.43 lakhs in unauthorized credit card transactions
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The Mumbai police and Cyber Cell immediately launched an investigation after the star alerted her bank over this suspicious overseas transaction notification.

Adding to this, As per the latest buzz, the incident came to light while Kirti was at a multiplex near Fun Republic Mall in Andheri West, Mumbai. During her visit, she as per reports received an alert on her mobile phone informing her of a foreign transaction worth $2,525 on Aeromexico Airlines through her credit card. The unexpected notification immediately raised concerns, as the star had not authorized any such payment.

Meanwhile, Realizing the transaction appeared suspicious, Kirti is shared to have contacted her bank's customer care helpline without delay. During the verification process, bank officials as per reports discovered that multiple unauthorized transactions had been carried out using her credit card. In total, four separate transactions had been processed without her consent, resulting in a financial loss of Rs 2,43,852.

Notably, As a precautionary measure, the bank immediately blocked the credit card to prevent any further misuse. The star later filed a complaint with the Amboli Police Station, following which an FIR was registered against unknown accused under relevant sections pertaining to cyber fraud.

As per the latest buzz, In her statement to the police, Kirti as per reports maintained that she had never shared her credit card password or confidential banking information with anyone. Investigators suspect that the fraud may have been executed through sophisticated digital methods, including the possible use of malware or spyware that compromised her phone or banking credentials. However, the exact modus operandi is yet to be determined.

In further updates, The investigation has now been taken up by the Cyber Cell, which is working alongside local police officials to identify the perpetrators. Authorities are as per reports examining bank reference numbers, transaction records, and other digital footprints in an effort to trace those involved in the fraudulent activity.
On top of that, The incident serves as another reminder of the growing threat posed by cybercrime, with online financial frauds increasingly targeting individuals through advanced hacking techniques.

On the professional front, Kirti Kulhari was last seen in the web-series Shekhar Home. title: Can you eat lettuce safely during the cyclospora outbreak? Advice from an infectious disease expert
body: Here's what's trending across the USA right now:
This article originally appeared on The Conversation .

Adding to this, Salads – along with other fresh produce – are some of the healthiest foods you can eat . Leafy greens are rich in vitamins A, C and K, folate, potassium and magnesium . They also contain lots of fiber, which supports a healthy gut microbiome , promotes fullness, helps regulate blood sugar , and may contribute to healthy aging and better cognitive function .

Meanwhile, But an ongoing 2026 outbreak of cyclosporiasis, caused by the cyclospora parasite, has sickened more than 11,500 people across the United States with explosive diarrhea and other gastrointestinal symptoms and has put a damper on salad consumption. A poll rolled out on July 26 reports that 40% of U.S. adults have cut down on buying and eating fresh produce. News of egg and blueberry recalls , plus an investigation into a new, separate cyclospora outbreak , has not helped.
Notably, WATCH: Cyclospora and salmonella outbreaks raise concerns about U.S. food safety

body: Here's what's trending across the USA right now:

Bald Eagle Big Bear eagle Jackie moved from ICU to regular hospital unit in encouraging recovery milestone Still, vet teams emphasize that Jackie is very sick and her progress does not mean she is out of danger.

Adding to this, Este artículo se ofrece en Español More good news is being shared about Big Bear's beloved bald eagle, Jackie, as she recovers from an illness at the Ojai Raptor Center. BIG BEAR LAKE, Calif. (KABC) -- More good news is being shared about Big Bear's beloved bald eagle, Jackie, as she recovers from an illness at the Ojai Raptor Center.

Meanwhile, In an update on Wednesday, the Ojai Raptor Center shared Jackie has been moved from the intensive care unit, where she required oxygen therapy, to one of the center's regular hospital care units.

Notably, "While this marks an encouraging milestone, she remains a very sick patient and continues to require intensive treatment and monitoring," vet teams wrote in a post on social media. "This is an encouraging step forward, but it does not mean she is out of danger."

As per the latest buzz, In all of their updates, the Ojai Raptor Center has referred to Jackie as "patient 26-519." In another post on social media Wednesday , vet teams clarified that California Department of Fish and Wildlife and U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service regulations state that rehabilitation animals "shall only be depicted in a public facing photograph or video under conditions that are consistent with the natural life history and behaviors of that species or showing the animal receiving appropriate medical treatment and only publicly referenced by intake number, common species or scientific name."
In further updates, So even though we know her as Jackie, she is "patient 26-519" at the rehabilitation center.

On top of that, After Jackie was rescued, experts shared she was anemic with inflammation affecting her kidneys . She received a life-saving blood transfusion from a fellow female eagle named Spirit, who is a resident at CALM Zoo in Bakersfield.
Jackie is one half of the beloved bald eagle couple captured on Friends of Big Bear Valley's (FOBBV) live nest camera with her partner, Shadow.

title: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash bring the spectacle and aura, but where are the emotions? | Ramayana trailer review
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Probably not since Baahubali has Indian cinema attempted to put its foot forward in such a grand fashion for the rest of the world, like Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana is trying. The movie is the costliest and grandest ever made on Indian shores. The first trailer - 4 minutes 10 seconds of it - wastes no time in showing you that. The grand scale, the dazzling visual effects, and that masterful score from the two maestros pull you in. But Ramayana has never been about the spectacle. It has always been about the connect you feel with the story, with the world, and with Lord Rama. There, this Ramayana trailer seemed to fall flat, as we saw stars on screens, not the Gods and demigods we grew up on. Ramayana trailer gets a lot right in its presentation, but sacrifices the core strength of Indian filmmaking - emotions.

Adding to this, Ramayana trailer review: Ranbir Kapoor in a still from the Nitesh Tiwari movie. What the Ramayana trailer gets right The scale is the one thing you cannot ignore with the trailer of Ramayana Part One. Everything from Ravana’s ascent as the king of Lanka to shots of Lord Rama’s exile are some of the grandest ever filmed in Indian cinema. The VFX complements them. The visual effects show a marked improvement since the Rama glimpse that was rolled out earlier this year. The battle sequences, particularly the shot of Airavata and Lord Indra falling, are spectacular, as are the designs of the daanavs and rakshasas. And then there is the Ramayana theme from Hans Zimmer and AR Rahman, which elevates the trailer to another plane. The one time I truly had goosebumps during the trailer was when the crescendo builds to ‘Dharti hai ambar hai..’ from the theme as Lord Rama vows to slay Ravana.

Meanwhile, Among the cast, Yash exudes Ravana’s aura and charisma. Both as the renegade who usurps Lanka from Kubera and the almighty Lankesh, he looks the part. But the problem his that his voice does not carry the weight of the man who rules the three lokas. Lara Dutta as Kaikeyi and Rakul Preet Singh as Surpanakha were my other standout performers in the trailer, both leaving a mark despite limited screen time. I would have wanted to see more of Ravie Dubey’s Lakshman, too, or at least hear him speak here. I will reserve my judgment on Sai Pallavi’s Sita when I see more of her, but she does appear to fit the part, to say the least.

Notably, But the biggest elephant in the room in this trailer, for me, is Ranbir Kapoor . He is a fine star, probably the best of his generation from Hindi cinema. To take on the role of Lord Rama in a movie of this scale, at this time, there is probably no other choice. But the problem is that throughout the trailer, I saw only Ranbir and not Rama. His dialogue delivery, which is otherwise standout, was very flat here. Some of the lines he gets here are to set the tone of the movie, but they seemed to be coming from another of Ranbir’s characters and not from Lord Rama . That makes the suspension of disbelief harder.

As per the latest buzz, Indian cinema has had a tricky relationship with trailers. For years, our trailers were just crunched versions of the movie. But that changed in the 90s with films like Darr and Raja Hindustani, as filmmakers cut trailers to entice the audience. Of late, Animal and Dhurandhar did the same. But Ramayana doesn’t take the less-is-more approach. Instead, it chooses to spell out the plot. And while we are all familiar with the story, we would have liked to see some things for the first time in the theatre. It still hides the vanaras' design, particularly Lord Hanuman's, so there is something to look forward to. But I do fear that the movie has already opened all its big cards.

In further updates, I am hopeful, if not totally optimistic. I will admit that Ramayana is my most anticipated movie of the year. I have been looking forward to it even more than a Dune Part Three or Avengers Doomsday (or King, closer to home). I really want this movie to be good because its success can open doors for Indian cinema that have been shut for decades. But mere anticipation and hope cannot sustain a movie. It needs substance. And I fear that may be lacking here.

On top of that, For the sake of Ramayana and its makers, I hope the movie is more than what the trailer shows. But come November, and Nitesh Tiwari, Namit Malhotra, and Ranbir Kapoor & co face their biggest agni pariksha. This movie does not depend on what critics say. It is Ramayana. It needs to connect with the masses. Failing that, it may be relegated to the unsavoury chapters of history. Look up Om Raut and Adipurush if there’s any doubt on that claim.

Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well. A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism. Work has led him to far off places like Japan and Jordan, as well as to the interiors of Haryana and the Indo-Pak border. He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic. A Rotten Tomatoes Certified Movie Critic, he is equally at home covering stories on ground as he is interviewing celebrities and studios, and sometimes prefers to shepherd teams in delivering traffic through the day. Even as his role has evolved from reporter to supervisor over the years, his first love remains writing (and of late, talking on camera). With a good understanding of cinema and its trends, and a keen eye for detail, he continues to spark conversations around showbiz for readers around the world. Read More

title: Sonu Sood reacts to Kangana Ranaut's 'Generation Gutter' remark on Gen Z: 'It is very shameful if she said that'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Kangana's 'Generation Gutter' label sparks backlash from Sonu Sood. (X) Sonu Sood responds to Kangana Ranaut’s remarks While interacting with the media, Sonu admitted that he had not watched Kangana ’s full statement. However, he stressed that actors owe their success to the audience, especially young people. “I haven’t heard her statement. But I feel that these young people are the ones who make actors, and they are the ones who help you reach this position,” he shared.

Adding to this, Emphasising the importance of public support, Sonu added, “As long as they stand by you, you will continue to thrive. If they are not with you, it becomes difficult. That’s why everyone should be taken along.”

Meanwhile, When asked specifically about Kangana referring to Gen Z as “Generation Gutter,” Sonu did not mince words. “If she has shared that, then I think it is very shameful. It should not have been shared,” he remarked.

Notably, The star also urged public figures to be careful with their words. “There is a saying, ‘Tol mol ke bol’ (weigh your words before speaking). It is very important to think carefully before you speak because the public is another form of God,” he shared.

As per the latest buzz, The row began after Kangana shared a series of Instagram Stories criticising a section of young people involved in the CJP protests. Calling them “Generation Gutter,” she accused them of glorifying “drugs, drinks, or endless body counts” while continuing to depend financially on their parents.

In further updates, She argued that independence has to be collected, writing that truly independent women make bold choices, build unconventional careers and take responsibility for their decisions because they are financially self-reliant.

On top of that, In another post, Kangana claimed that many of the so-called “westernised” young women had “nothing to offer to the system” and criticised them for, in her view, seeking an independent lifestyle without earning it.
Kangana’s remarks have sparked a war of words with CJP spokesperson Saurav Das and founder Abhijeet Dipke, with the debate continuing to play out on social media.

Today, the grand trailer of the mythological epic was unveiled at brahma muhurat, and since then, it has become a trending topic. At the recent San Diego Comic-Con 2026 trailer launch, actors Ranbir Kapoor , Yash, along with director Nitesh Tiwari and producer Namit Malhotra explained to Fandom why Ramayana is a story that will resonate with people all over the world irrespective of their experience with Indian cinema.

Adding to this, Namit Malhotra explains why Ramayana is India's biggest cinematic spectacle: 'It will entertain and enlighten'. Namit Malhotra compares Ramayana to Hollywood blockbusters When the interviewer admitted never having seen an Indian movie, the cast first asked about their favourite movies. While explaining the scale and vision behind Ramayana, producer Namit Malhotra compared the movie to some of Hollywood's biggest fantasy and action spectacles, while stressing that its biggest strength lies in its emotional storytelling.

Meanwhile, He shared, “Ramayana is like Avatar meets gladiator in the world of Lord of the Rings like so if you can put that together. Lord Vishnu, who's the protector of all life, he has to come as an avatar to bring balance and restore life back.”

Notably, He further explained, “So god descends as a human and goes through his life in a in a human form to really understand how humans feel ultimately to fulfil their duty. Then it's mounted in the back of this massive spectacle woven into the fabric of the screenplay. It's all about emotions. The underdog story of sacrifice, of revenge and absolutely cutting edge execution. It's a story which not only is going to entertain you but also going to enlighten you.”

As per the latest buzz, The trailer begins with Yash's Ravana dominating his kingdom. He shows his power and menacing avatar. Then, the story moves on to see Lord Vishnu take the guise of Lord Rama. Arun Govil stars as King Dashrath and introduces Rama, who promises to protect humans at the expense of his life. The trailer then shows the important events of Ramayana including the marriage between Rama and Sita, their 14 years' period of exile, and Sita's kidnapping. The trailer's pivotal scene comes when Lord Rama tells Lakshman that he will do everything to rescue Sita, by saying, “If Ravana is the king of three worlds, then he will have to face his death in the three worlds.”

In further updates, Ramayana: Part One stars Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, Yash, Ravi Dubey, Vivek Oberoi, Saurabh Sachdeva and Rakul Preet Singh, among others. The first installment is set for a worldwide theatrical rollout on November 8 during Diwali, while the second part will arrive in 2027.

title: CJP praises Ayesha Khan for showing solidarity with students and joining Mumbai protests
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Dhurandhar star Ayesha Khan was detained by Mumbai Police on July 22 while attempting to join the nationwide student protests over the NEET paper leak scandal, spearheaded by the Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ). A week after news of her detention made headlines, the political outfit has come out in her support, praising the star's courage for standing in solidarity with the students' movement.

Adding to this, A month-long protest had already been underway at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, led by the CJP and social and environmental activist Sonam Wangchuk , who had been on a hunger strike demanding education reforms. The movement escalated on July 20 with a “ Sansad Chalo ” march in Delhi, which inspired solidarity protests across several cities the same day. Tensions flared when police resorted to lathi charges and tear gas to disperse demonstrators, triggering widespread outrage. In the aftermath of the crackdown, several prominent voices from the entertainment industry came out in support of the protesting students.

Meanwhile, Among the many people detained during the demonstrations was Dhurandhar star Ayesha Khan, who was forcibly escorted into a police van and taken to Mumbai's Worli Police Station. On July 23, the star, who rose to fame with her appearance in the song “Shararat” from Dhurandhar, shared a video filmed inside the police station. In the clip, she alleged that Mumbai Police had detained her merely for standing on the road.

Notably, Now, a week later, with the protests beginning to subside, Ayesha shared a workout video on Instagram, where the Cockroach Janta Party's official handle publicly lauded her for supporting the students' movement. The party's comment read, “Thank you Ayesha for standing with students and supporting their voice. Your courage and commitment to their cause show the importance of standing up for justice and education.”

As per the latest buzz, Ayesha Khan was detained by Mumbai Police on July 22 while attempting to join a protest held in solidarity with students demanding education reforms. The star later shared a series of videos from inside the police van and Mumbai's Worli Police Station, alleging that she had been taken into custody despite not having raised any slogans. The 23-year-old star looked visibly shaken in a video she shared on her Instagram stories, which showed her getting pulled into a police van as she repeatedly asked the officers why she was being detained.

In further updates, In a video shared on Instagram later, Ayesha recounted the incident, saying that she, her brother and a group of friends had gathered on the road to join a protest scheduled to take place in Dadar at 4 pm. According to the star, they had only just arrived when a police officer informed them that they were not allowed to protest at the location. Before they could even respond or begin a conversation, the police allegedly pulled her brother and a friend into a van. As Ayesha stood on the road trying to process what was happening and decide what to do next, she too was detained.
On top of that, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ayesha Khan (@ayeshaakhan_official)

She continued, “At least 15 police personnel – 10 men and five women – came to me and my two other friends and told us we had to get into the van. I was simply asking why, as we were just standing on the road. We hadn't shared anything, hadn't started anything, weren't showing any placards, and weren't shouting any slogans. We were just waiting for my brother and friends. There was no answer as to why we were being pulled in…no accountability, nothing. No one gave any answer, and they brought us far from Dadar to Worli…What about the people who used force on the ground, who pushed me, my friends, and my brother? What was our fault? Just being there?”

title: Cornucopian Euthanized Following Bing Crosby Injury
body: Here's what's trending across the USA right now:
Cornucopian following his victory in the San Carlos Stakes at Santa Anita Park

Adding to this, After sustaining an injury during the Bing Crosby Stakes (G1) July 25 at Del Mar , dual graded stakes winner Cornucopian 🔥 was euthanized, Tom Ryan of co-owner SF Racing revealed on X July 26.

Meanwhile, Cornucopian had raced in a stalking position early in the 6-furlong contest and was beginning to make a move toward the leaders when jockey Juan Hernandez began to pull him up around the quarter pole. California equine medical director Dr. Jeff Blea told Horse Racing Nation that the 4-year-old colt had injured his right-front fetlock. He was loaded into an ambulance and taken back to his barn for further evaluation, but ultimately the injury proved too severe.

Notably, "Heavy hearts today. Yesterday, our brilliant colt Cornucopian sustained a catastrophic injury," Ryan shared in the post. "We worked very closely with our veterinary team, and after hearing every expert opinion available, the kindest and clearest decision was to let him go with dignity. He was a brilliant colt with a huge heart and a partnership and fan base that loved him dearly."

As per the latest buzz, Bred in Kentucky by Three Chimneys Farm and Whisper Hill Farm, Cornucopian brought $1.1 million at the 2023 Keeneland September Yearling Sale when consigned by Gainesway. He raced for the partnership of SF Racing, Starlight Racing, Madaket Stables, Stonestreet Stables, Bashor Racing, Determined Stables, Robert Masterson, Front Row Club, Waves Edge Capital, Catherine Donovan, and Hill 'n' Dale Equine Holdings. He was trained by Hall of Famer Bob Baffert.

In further updates, Cornucopian caught plenty of eyes with a scintillating 5 3/4-length debut win over 6 furlongs at Oaklawn Park in February 2025. He would then stretch out to 1 1/8 miles and finish fourth in the Arkansas Derby (G1) in his second start.

On top of that, Returned to sprint competition at 4, Cornucopian continued to display his brilliance with a 2 3/4-length win in the San Carlos Stakes (G3) at Santa Anita Park in March and 1 1/4-length triumph in the Aristides Stakes (G3) at Churchill Downs in May. Those credentials made him a 6-5 favorite in Saturday's Bing Crosby.
With a record of 4-1-0 from eight starts, Cornucopian collected $462,655.

title: Kirti Kulhari targeted by cyber criminals, ₹2.44 lakh stolen through unauthorised card transactions
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Cyber scams continue to hit people in the country, including celebrities. Bollywood star Kirti Kulhari was of late a victim of what is allegedly a credit card scam. Cyber criminals allegedly used her credit card details to conduct unauthorised transactions abroad worth ₹ 2.44 lakh. Upon lodging a complaint, Amboli police in Mumbai have lodged a case against unknown persons.

Adding to this, Kirti Kulhari duped in cyber scam, fraudsters siphon off ₹2.44 lakh through credit card. Kirti Kulhari's credit card allegedly misused for foreign transactions According to ABP News, Police shared that the incident happened on the night of July 24 when the 43-year-old star, who stays on Yari Road, Versova, went out to watch a movie at a multiplex in Andheri West. During her journey to the cinemas, she got an alert from her bank about a foreign currency transaction on her account.

Meanwhile, The alert mentioned that a transfer of US$2,525 was done to the Aeromexico Airlines through her credit card. Kirti was shocked and quickly informed her bank’s customer care regarding the same. After checking her account and details with the bank, it was as per reports found that four separate transactions had been processed using her credit card. Together, the unauthorized payments amounted to more than ₹ 2.43 lakh. The bank immediately blocked her credit card inorder to stop any further misuse.

Notably, Preliminary investigations have shown that Kirti had not revealed her card PIN or any other banking details to anyone. It has made investigators speculate that her card details might have been stolen through a technical means as opposed to getting direct access.

As per the latest buzz, They are currently investigating if the information might have leaked via the mobile phone, online account, or any other digital network. The banking history, transactions, and digital trails are being analyzed to find out who is behind the scenes. The Amboli Police, along with the cyber experts, are still investigating.

In further updates, As far as the professional front goes, Kirti Kulhari of late shared that she had completed shooting for her debut feature movie as producer which will certainly be one of the landmarks of her career. Some of the popular films and television shows in which the star has been seen include: Uri: The Surgical Strike, Mission Mangal (2019), Four More Shots Please!, Criminal Justice and Human. title: Ramayana trailer decoded: From Airavat to Pushpak Vimana, 4 major mythological details you need to know
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The trailer of Ramayana , directed by Nitesh Tiwari, finally rolled out on July 30 during brahma muhurat and has already been creating buzz across all the platforms on the internet. Most of the discussions about the trailer revolve around the appearance of Ranbir Kapoor in the role of Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Goddess Sita, the menacing depiction of Ravana played by Yash, and the intense music score provided by Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman.

Adding to this, Ramayana trailer isn't just about Ranbir Kapoor and Yash; these hidden details deserve your attention. However, there is much more than the aforementioned in the trailer. Apart from the presence of the cast and grand visuals of the movie, the makers have incorporated some mythological references that give an interesting context to the story. Here's a closer look at the mythological details in the Ramayana trailer.

Meanwhile, One of the significant moments in the trailer shows a giant white elephant in a grand aerial battle. And it is believed that the elephant is Airavat, the divine mount of Lord Indra. According to Hindu mythology, Airavat is the elephant that appeared during the Samudra Manthan and was made the celestial elephant of Lord Indra, king of the Devas (gods). It is mostly described as a majestic white elephant with multi-tusks/trunks and golden armour.

Notably, It feels that the appearance of the elephant in the trailer is likely more than just a visual spectacle. The scene could be hinting at Ravana's conquest of Swarga Loka, one of the epic's significant chapters. It may even tease the battle in which Ravana's son Meghnad defeats Lord Indra, earning the title Indrajit (Conqueror of Indra).

As per the latest buzz, This also raises the stakes of the battles that we will witness in the movie. Instead of presenting Ravana as merely the king of Lanka, the trailer suggests he is a ruler whose power extends to challenging the gods themselves, underlining the scale of the conflict long before the central battle with Lord Rama begins.

In further updates, One of the visual elements featured in the trailer which stands out is a gigantic flying structure flying in the sky. The structure is shared to be none other than the famous Pushpak Vimana.

On top of that, As per Hindu mythology, the Vimana (airborne palace) was created by Vishwakarma, the celestial architect, for Lord Brahma. He then gave the Vimana as a gift to Kubera, the God of wealth and half-brother of Ravana. However, Ravana stole the Pushpak Vimana from Kubera after defeating him. In the epic, Pushpak Vimana is described as a flying palace which can fly at the speed of thought and expand to accommodate any number of people.
Apart from serving as a mode of transportation in the trailer, the Pushpak Vimana also seems to represent the opulence and grandeur of Lanka. And how much Ravana boasted about his kingdom.

title: Ramayana trailer FINALLY out: Sunny Deol missing but Yash AMAZES as Ravana; Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi IMPRESS in the grand 3D spectacle
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The earlier promotional asset focused on Lord Rama, played by Ranbir Kapoor, while the trailer introduces several other characters. However, the character which dominates the proceedings is Ravana, played by Yash. The trailer opens with him, and the manner in which he has been presented is sure to amaze viewers. His ferocious avatar and action sequences particularly stand out. Several actors have portrayed Ravana in the past, but Yash’s interpretation is distinctive, without a shred of doubt.

Adding to this, Meanwhile, Lord Rama, the Maryada Purushottam, also gets due prominence. Ranbir Kapoor’s performance appears graceful and divine, serving as the perfect contrast to Ravana’s arrogant persona.

Meanwhile, Apart from Yash, Sai Pallavi also makes a striking appearance. As Sita, she appears suitably poised and convincing. Lara Dutta, Rakul Preet Singh, Ravie Dubey, Arun Govil and Vivek Oberoi also make their presence felt. Sadly, Sunny Deol’s Lord Hanuman does not feature in the four-minute-plus trailer. Nevertheless, there are no complaints, as the trailer offers enough to heighten the audience’s excitement for Ramayana .

Notably, The scale is spectacular, while the 3D effects are impressive. A particular sequence featuring Airavata, the divine white elephant, is especially stunning. Yet, a few shortcomings remain. The grandeur is comparable to that of Baahubali and perhaps does not surpass it. This may not be a major concern, but with reports suggesting that more than Rs. 1,000 crores have been spent on the movie, one would have expected the scale and visual quality to be a notch higher. Thankfully, this is only a minor hiccup and is unlikely to affect the hype in any way.

As per the latest buzz, The trailer is certain to attract massive viewership, and moviegoers will also get an opportunity to experience it in all its glory on the big screen with Spider-Man: Brand New Day . The superhero saga is expected to record the biggest opening ever for a Hollywood movie in India. As a result, the Ramayana trailer will receive widespread exposure in cinemas, which is exactly how a spectacle of this magnitude deserves to be experienced. The trailer serves its purpose, and it goes without saying that the movie is set to take a thunderous start during the Festival of Lights.

In further updates, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. It is directed by Nitesh Tiwari of Dangal (2016) fame and produced by Namit Malhotra. The music is composed by A R Rahman and Hans Zimmer. It's a two-part saga with the first part releasing on Diwali 2026. As for the second part, it'll arrive on the big screen on Diwali 2027.

title: Ramayana trailer reactions: Praise for Yash, mixed verdict on Ranbir Kapoor, internet asks where is Sunny Deol's Hanuman
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The official trailer of Ramayana , Nitesh Tiwari’s adaptation of the epic, was unveiled today at 4:15 am, during the brahma muhurat. The trailer gave the much awaited glimpse into the world of the mythological epic which introduces Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Ravi Dubey as Lakshman and Yash in the role of Ravana.

Adding to this, Ramayana trailer sparks buzz: Stunning visuals, Yash's Ravana shine, Hanuman's absence surprises followers. What happens in the trailer The trailer opens with Ravana (Yash) arriving at a palace and knocking on its massive doors, only to receive a hostile welcome. Unfazed, he responds with brute force and declares that it marks the beginning of "Ravana Raaj."

Meanwhile, As fear spreads among gods and kings over the darkness that lies ahead, Lord Vishnu is reborn on Earth as Prince Ram, the son of Ayodhya's King Dasharatha (Arun Govil). The trailer then follows Ram's early journey as he fights demons to protect his people, standing alongside his younger brother Lakshman (Ravi Dubey).

Notably, The story soon shifts to one of the defining moments of the Ramayana. A promise made to Queen Kaikeyi (Lara Dutta) forces King Dasharatha to send Ram into exile for 14 years. Refusing to stay behind, Sita (Sai Pallavi) tells Ram that she will accompany him on the difficult journey, setting the stage for the events that follow.

As per the latest buzz, Unlike the teaser, the trailer keeps its attention on the kingdoms of Ayodhya and Lanka, highlighting their grandeur through elaborate sets and rich visuals. It also cuts back on mythical creatures and fantastical elements, choosing instead to focus on the central characters and the emotional weight of the story.

In further updates, The dialogues, performances and overall dramatic tone make this trailer a much stronger introduction than the earlier teaser, which had drawn criticism for its visual effects. Interestingly, there are no glimpses of Lord Hanuman, suggesting that the makers may be saving his much-awaited appearance for the second part. Overall, the trailer promises a more grounded yet visually rich retelling of one of India's most celebrated epics while building excitement for what's to come.

On top of that, View this post on Instagram Followers praise the visuals and scale A section of social media users couldn't stop praising the trailer, calling it one of the most visually impressive projects to come out of Indian cinema. One user on X, formerly Twitter, wrote, “Excellent VFX- Top notch visuals- Grand background score- Superb colour grading #Ramayana Trailer is not just a trailer–it’s absolute cinema.”
Another viewer felt the trailer was much bigger than a promotional video and wrote, “This isn't just a trailer. It's a statement from Indian cinema.”

title: ‘Children of Blood and Bone’ Author Tomi Adeyemi Left Film’s Set ‘Sobbing,’ Calls It the ‘Worst Thing I’ve Had to Live Through’ and ‘I Never Want to Hear About It Again’
body: Here's what's trending across the USA right now:

Variety Plus Icon Click to expand the Mega Menu Plus Icon Click to Expand Search Input Variety Plus Icon Read Next: The Bruin Theater in Westwood Village to Reopen: ‘It’s a Magical Place’ Home Movie News Jul 29, 2026 1:59pm PT ‘Children of Blood and Bone’ Author Tomi Adeyemi Left Movie’s Set ‘Sobbing,’ Calls It the ‘Worst Thing I’ve Had to Live Through’ and ‘I Never Want to Hear About It Again’

Adding to this, Tomi Adeyemi , author of the novel “ Children of Blood and Bone ,” shared the soon-to-release Paramount movie adaptation of her book was “the worst thing I have ever had to live through” and “I never want to hear about this project again” in a five-minute video posted on Wednesday.

Meanwhile, Adeyemi, who co-wrote the screenplay for the movie, had previously spoken out about how she wouldn’t watch the “Children of Blood and Bone” movie based on her African fantasy novel after being on set for its production. Related Stories YouTube Ad Sales Keep Growing at Healthy Clip, Rising 13% to $11 Billion in Q2 Peacock to Be Included in YouTube Premium Subscription Bundle Starting in 2027

Notably, “What I’m about to share is not a secret to the people involved,” she shared in the social media clip. “It’s a reality that I’ve had to live with for about a year and a half, and everyone involved, at least at the highest level, has been made aware of this reality, and they haven’t done anything to make it better. If anything, they’ve only antagonized me, and I accept that. But I also accept if I don’t say something, I think it’s just going to be worse.” Popular on Variety

As per the latest buzz, Adeyemi alleged that she left the “Children of Blood and Bone” set “hyperventilating and sobbing” and that she is “still being antagonized behind the scenes.” Representatives for Adeyemi, Paramount and director Gina Prince-Bythewood did not immediately respond to Variety’s requests for comment.

In further updates, “I’m not going to speak on what I endured to make it through the young adult trilogy, and I’m not going to speak about everything that I also suffered through or endured to make the adaptation a reality,” Adeyemi shared. “I’m actually only going to speak about what happened after I left that set of my own movie adaptation, hyperventilating and sobbing. There are many witnesses, so it’s not really a secret. I came back to America and suffered such severe somatic pain and so many panic attacks. I knew it was so bad that I would never ever be able to watch this movie, and I made peace with that.”

On top of that, “But as it is being marketed,” Adeyemi continued, referencing the trailer which launched on Tuesday, “And as I am still being antagonized behind the scenes, which is where I hoped all of this would stay, it’s become apparent to me that reality needs to at least be made known, so that you guys can understand how this movie, which I worked on to make it a little better for us to be alive, is also the worst thing I have ever had to live through.”

Earlier this month in a since-deleted TikTok video, Adeyemi posted what appeared to be a group chat that included “Children of Blood and Bone” star Amandla Stenberg. Adeyemi wrote, "Do not ever use my name in an interview or video again. Do not text me. Do not call me” and appeared to block Stenberg, according to the L.A. Times. Stenberg had previously received backlash from book followers over her casting as Princess Amari due to allegations of colorism.

Meanwhile, With gods and kings fearful of what the future holds, Lord Vishnu takes a new, human avatar as the son of Ayodhya’s King Dasharatha, played by Arun Govil. Ranbir Kapoor as Prince Ram slays demons to protect his land and people with help from his brother Lakshman (Ravi Dubey). However, a promise made to Kaikeyi (Lara Dutta) sends him to a vanvaas of 14 years. His wife, Sita (Sai Pallavi) expresses her wish to go with him.

Notably, The trailer includes fewer mythical animals and demons and shows more the oppulence of Ayodhya and Lanka. The drama and the dialogues make the trailer a far better watch that the teaser, which was marred by bad CGI.
As per the latest buzz, There is no mention or visuals of Lord Hanuman in the trailer, perhaps reserved for the second part.
In further updates, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Namit Malhotra (@iamnamitmalhotra)

On top of that, The movie's music brings together Oscar winners A.R. Rahman and Hans Zimmer for the first time, while DNEG is leading the visual effects. In another major milestone, T-Series bought the music rights for both parts of the movie in a record-breaking ₹ 75 crore rupees deal with producer Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios.

Ramayana is the latest adaptation of Valmiki's epic, one of the world's oldest pieces of literature. It tells the story of Lord Rama, the incarnation of Lord Vishnu (played by Ranbir Kapoor), and his battle against the asura king Ravana (Yash) after the latter abducts his wife, Sita (Sai Pallavi). The epic is one of the most familiar stories in the Indian subcontinent and is revered by Hindus as a sacred text.

title: Fortnite Reload x The Simpsons Details
body: Here's what's trending across the USA right now:

The beloved Springfield map is returning to Fortnite on July 30, 2026, but this time, it's in Reload. There's a brand-new John Wick-inspired POI, an exclusive Sprite, more enemies to kill, and more. Here's everything we know about the Fortnite Reload The Simpsons collaboration and map.

Adding to this, Not only is the entire Springfield map returning, but it brings a new POI with it: The Confidential, AKA The Continental from John Wick. The classic hotel serves as neutral territory for the criminal underworld in the movies, and in Fortnite, it's also a no-violence zone.

Meanwhile, Once inside The Confidential, you'll gain passive healing , giving you a place to shelter if you need a patch up. If you were a fan of the limited-time Delulu mode, you'll be happy to know that proximity chat is also enabled inside so you can strike up a friendly conversation with your enemies if you'd like.

Notably, While The Confidential has a strict no fighting policy, that's not to say you can't shoot at other players inside... But there are consequences. If you damage another player while in the building, you'll become " excommunicado " and your location will be revealed to everyone on the map, making you an instant target.

As per the latest buzz, Only one player can be excommunicado at a time, and that player will have unlimited stamina and increased reload speed . If you eliminate an excommunicado player, they'll drop rare loot and 1,500 Gold.

In further updates, There's a new Sprite in Fortnite: John Wick. Based on the deadly assassin himself, the John Wick Sprite is exclusive to Reload . Once you've found and extracted the John Wick Sprite, he'll be usable in other Battle Royale modes such as Zero Build.

On top of that, The John Wick Sprite is the only Sprite that can be used in Reload, and having it equipped reveals nearby opponents to both you and your teammates after you’ve knocked or eliminated another player.

You can get the John Wick Sprite by either finding it in a chest, eliminating another player that has it equipped, or by winning a match. If you find it during a match, you'll need to use a Reload Portable Extractor to extract it and add it to your collection.

Stocks tumbled for a myriad of reasons Wednesday, but mostly because the bond market signaled the Federal Reserve could be falling behind on the inflation fight as the central bank chose to keep interest rates unchanged.

Adding to this, The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed 1,153.18 points lower, or 2.19%, at 51,594.14 for its worst decline since April 2025. The S&P 500 slid 1.52% to end the day at 7,316.15. The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.74% to 24,442.94, ending the session more than 10% off its all-time high.

Meanwhile, The Fed kept to the sidelines in its latest rate decision , and the bond market responded with the 10-year Treasury yield jumping 7 basis points to above 4.67%. The 30-year Treasury yield soared 10 basis points to above 5.2%, hitting its highest level since 2007.
Notably, Three officials wanted a hike, but the Fed still stood pat on rates. And Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's tough talk failed to convince the bond market.

As per the latest buzz, "I want to stress, of course, that decisions by this committee matter a great deal, and where necessary and appropriate, we will not hesitate to act," Warsh shared during his press conference.

In further updates, "If you really want to get to 2%, I think you have to raise interest rates," shared DoubleLine's Jeffrey Gundlach on CNBC's " Closing Bell ," noting that the jump in yields after the Fed decision was sending a message to Warsh.

On top of that, "The long bond yield went up significantly after the press conference because the bond market vigilantes are saying, 'If you really want us to believe your rhetoric, you've got to start acting,'" shared Gundlach.

Adding to inflation concerns was a jump in oil prices after President Donald Trump told a Fox News reporter that the U.S. will be hitting Iran "hard" in response to surprise attacks on troops in the Middle East. West Texas Intermediate crude futures advanced more than 6% to settle at $84.46 a barrel.

title: 'Reports I'm gone every weekend are grossly misstated': SPD chief defends how often he leaves Seattle
body: Here's what's trending across the USA right now:
The Jake and Spike Show, weekdays from 12 p.m. - 3 p.m.

Adding to this, Following the Bite of Seattle shooting at the Seattle Center that killed three and injured at least four others, city leaders have held multiple press conferences to relay details of the investigation to the media, with one specific conference turning into “a scuffle.”

Meanwhile, Jake Skorheim and Spike O’Neill, co-hosts of “ The Jake and Spike Show ” on KIRO Newsradio, recapped an exchange between Seattle Police Department Chief Shon Barnes and a reporter who asked why the chief wasn’t in town during the shooting.

Notably, “There’s two stories happening simultaneously. One is the shooting, and then also the victims,” Jake shared. “The response from local officials is a whole nother side of the story, and that’s what, unfortunately, these press conferences have devolved into. Chief Shon Barnes, who was out of town when it happened, as has been reported, is frequently out of town because he is not originally from Seattle. His family’s in Chicago. When you have a job like protecting a city, most people would assume that you would be here most of the time, aside from vacation, which happened.

As per the latest buzz, “He was asked about that yesterday after the press conference, and it turned into kind of a scuffle,” Jake continued. “Barnes was literally walked out of the room by people who got in between him and this reporter for asking these questions.”

In further updates, At the press conference, Barnes was in conversation with Connor Nash, a reporter for The South Seattle Emerald , who had asked the chief about reports that he is not in town often.

On top of that, “I have been working as hard as I can for this city from the day I got here. Do you got that?” Barnes shared. “No, no, no, you listen to me. Their reports are wrong. You understand? I work …”

“Chief Barnes is getting very passionate, and it sounds kind of confrontational to me,” Jake shared. “He was asked about [the encounter] today. When you’re responding to questions like this, you’re not winning the game of PR. Responding to questions about the way that you’re interacting with reporters, when people really should be caring about getting the gunman who’s still on the loose.”

title: As extreme heat grips the South and West, here's how to stay safe
body: Here's what's trending across the USA right now:

The U.S. is sweating out its third major heat dome in a month, with some 70 million people affected in an area stretching from roughly New Mexico to North Carolina, covering much of the South and part of the Midwest. This latest extreme weather is again raising the risk of heat-related illness, particularly for millions of people in the affected region who lack easy access to air conditioning.
Adding to this, Daytime temperatures are reaching the 100s in many places, with the "feels like" temperature or heat index — which factors in humidity — even higher.

Meanwhile, Climate Why certain medications can increase your risk in the heat A heat dome is defined as a large, high-pressure atmospheric system that acts as a lid to trap hot air and humidity over an area for days or even weeks. "It's just a very strong area of high pressure. Under that, there's sinking air. Sinking air compresses, it warms, it heats up, and it also dries the air out," according to AccuWeather meteorologist Reneé Duff.

Notably, Later in the week, "the main core of heat [is] shifting a bit farther west" with most of the 90-degree heat shifting to California and parts of the Four Corners region, Duff says. Friday, Saturday and Sunday will see record or near-record temperatures of about 115 degrees around Phoenix, she says.

As per the latest buzz, "A lot of states that are being impacted by the highest temperatures are in severe to extreme drought ," she adds. They include New Mexico, Colorado, Utah, Wyoming and Idaho, Duff says, where "the drier ground lends to higher temperatures."

In further updates, Marc Chenard, a National Weather Service meteorologist, says the extreme heat advisories and warnings that remained in effect through at least Tuesday were concentrated in Arkansas, Tennessee and parts of the Gulf Coast.

On top of that, He acknowledges that the intensity of these heat waves is unusual, with a prime factor likely being El Niño, the cyclical warming of the Pacific Ocean that increases the odds of warmer temperatures in North America.

Climate 'We're screaming into the void.' Across the U.S., heat keeps breaking records "Typically we'll have a couple of these and they may kind of move around through the summer," Chenard says. "But, each one of these has been pretty strong, like the strength has been pretty impressive, and so just the persistence and strength certainly seems anomalous."

title: What time does League Classic release on your server?
body: Here's what's trending across the USA right now:
Image: Riot Games Jump Links What time does League Classic rollout on your server? League Classic, explained League Classic is sending League of Legends back to the past on Wednesday, July 29 .

Adding to this, Players will be able to experience the old days of League as champions, items, runes, masteries, and even the map will be reverted to their previous versions. Typically, you can expect League of Legends updates when the patch goes live, but Classic won't be available right away. Instead, it'll be rolled out at the same time around the world.
Meanwhile, Here's what time League Classic will be rolled out on your server.
Notably, Update (July 29): The rollout time for League Classic has been pushed back to 2 p.m. EDT. We've updated this guide to reflect the change.

As per the latest buzz, League Classic will launch a little differently than usual. Rather than going live at the same time as the patch, it will be rolled out globally at 2 p.m. EDT on Wednesday, July 29, for every server (minus China) according to the League Classic website . Here's when League Classic will go live in your time zone:

In further updates, League Classic is bringing back the "greatest hits" of the early seasons. Veteran players will be able to relive their nostalgic memories, while newer players can see a bit of history. The "back to the past" game mode uses Season 3 as a framework with champions using their old kits and the map looking like its old self. However, it won't be a one-to-one replica. Instead, it will be a bit more modernized. It'll include a bunch of quality of life updates that have come to League of Legends over the past 17 years.

On top of that, Image: Riot Games As League Classic is returning to a previous era, a majority of the new champions will not be coming back, as they didn't exist. Classic will start out with 60 champions, 40 being the original and 20 being handpicked. Champions will be added through The Council, which is essentially the League Classic player base. Players will be able to vote for which champions join Classic next. In the past, champs would come out every two weeks, but in Classic , champs might be joining more frequently .

In the past, champions were without a doubt "broken." In League Classic , champions will be slightly adjusted, but if anything is extremely overpowered, you won't have to worry about it for long, as Classic will be receiving its own updates. Classic will have its own development team, and it won't follow in the exact footsteps that League of Legends did in the past.

title: In Mason Gooding’s 650-Square-Foot “Tree House” Apartment, Bold Colors Bring the Outdoors In
body: Here's what's trending across the USA right now:

The vintage Danish 1940s chair from 1stDibs was reupholstered in a chocolate brown shearling, which Gooding says “conjures up ideas of comfort as well as deliciousness.” The ottoman was custom-made to match. The mirror is Soho Home .

Adding to this, “It coincided with my love of culture and the way I engage with it now in my burgeoning 30s. I wanted a community that was accessible just outside my door,” says Gooding, who got his first taste of life in the Big Apple while attending NYU. The I Want Your Sex star hit Zillow, and a few weeks later, his manager sent him a listing that seemed “too good to be true.” The roughly 650-square-foot apartment was in need of a renovation, but it was surrounded by greenery from a neighboring courtyard; Gooding jumped on the opportunity to invest in the charming urban “tree house.”
Meanwhile, Underneath it all is a rug from Ernesta to tie together the masculine but cozy palette of browns and greens in the living room. The fireplace tiles are from Clé .

Notably, The 72 Hours star says he is “ignorant to design in a lot of ways” and enlisted AD PRO Directory designer Claudia Roth of Claudia Allegra Interiors early on in the process. Roth, however, gives him much more credit. “If you saw the initial photos, you would have to see a lot of potential in it,” she says. “The way the previous owners had it—it was clearly untouched for years—wasn’t optimizing the space well at all, especially in the bathroom and the kitchen. And luckily, Mason really saw that there was potential.”
As per the latest buzz, Gooding enjoys having coffee on his fire escape, where he can hear the bells from a nearby church. “I’m a romantic,” he says.

In further updates, In their first design meeting, Gooding referenced the Ralph Lauren store in SoHo, saying he wanted a space that was “comfortable as well as compelling.” Roth took this as permission to go bold with color and pattern, and Gooding proved himself to be anything but a risk-averse client. “He was never afraid of color. Sometimes we’d show him something more neutral, and he was like, ‘Let’s push it. Let’s go dark brown. Let’s go green on the fireplace,’” recalls Roth.

On top of that, Two House of Léon Ingresso accent chairs provide a sculptural moment around the Williams Sonoma coffee tables. In the dining area, House of Léon chairs reupholstered in Holland & Sherry’s Wild Pony fabric and a CB2 table sit under an Urban Electric chandelier.

The tiny wood-clad kitchen became a more spacious aubergine jewel box; the bathroom became a moody sanctuary. The oversized living room fireplace was pared back to save space, though its green tiles make a bold statement. Millwork was added to cover radiators and air conditioners and to add ample shelving to the second bedroom, which Gooding uses as a den.

title: COVID Study Supports Antiviral Use in Kidney Transplant Recipients
body: Here's what's trending across the USA right now:

Add MedPage Today on Google MedpageToday Key Takeaways Kidney transplant recipients face severe COVID-19 risks but often are excluded from key antiviral trials. In a target trial emulation, starting remdesivir (Veklury) soon after a COVID diagnosis was associated with a 47% lower risk of graft failure or death at 1 year. Early remdesivir also was associated with a 42% lower risk of cardiovascular events. Kidney transplant recipients with COVID-19 who received remdesivir (Veklury) early had a lower risk of graft loss, a target trial emulation study found.

Adding to this, Compared with no remdesivir, initiation of the antiviral within 7 days of a COVID diagnosis was associated with a 47% lower risk of graft failure or death at 1 year in an analysis that employed clone-censor-weight adjustment (HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.31-0.92), reported Nitipong Permpalung, MD, MPH, of Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine in Baltimore, and colleagues.

Meanwhile, This association was generally consistent across clinically relevant subgroups, according to the findings in JAMA Network Open , and early remdesivir was also associated with a 42% lower risk of cardiovascular events (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.35-0.98).

Notably, "The main message for clinicians is to act early," Permpalung told MedPage Today . "When a kidney transplant recipient develops COVID-19 symptoms or tests positive, the patient should contact the transplant team promptly, and antiviral treatment should be considered before the illness becomes severe."

As per the latest buzz, Remdesivir is an important option particularly when an oral antiviral is not clinically suitable, he added. "However, our findings do not mean that every kidney transplant recipient should automatically receive remdesivir," Permpalung cautioned. "Treatment should be individualized based on the timing of infection, the patient's clinical risk, drug interactions, safety, preferences, and access to treatment."

In further updates, Kidney transplant recipients have a high risk of severe COVID-19 due to chronic immunosuppression, impaired vaccine responses, and comorbidities. "Mortality in hospitalized kidney transplant recipients during the early pandemic ranged from 20% to 32%, declining to 1% to 4% during the Omicron wave, likely due to vaccination, prior infection, and improved treatment," the researchers wrote.

On top of that, "Prevention and treatment should be viewed as complementary," Permpalung emphasized. " Vaccination remains the first layer of protection , but kidney transplant recipients may still have breakthrough infections because of their immunosuppression. When infection occurs, there should already be a plan for rapid testing, contacting the transplant team, and accessing antiviral treatment."

Although CDC guidelines recommend early antiviral therapy for patients at high risk of COVID-19 progression, many supporting trials excluded patients with severe kidney impairment and transplant recipients.

title: Trump has singled out us Canadians for special treatment in his tariff war – there is no choice but to get nasty
body: Here's what's trending across the USA right now:

T hough many hate to admit it, Canadians have long wished for more attention from the US. Well, we’re getting it now. And it turns out that President Trump and some of his top supporters in the Maga movement don’t much like us.

Adding to this, The first big hint was when he started talking about annexing us , saying we couldn’t survive without American support. But the most recent example of Trump’s dislike for Canada can be seen in his latest tariff policies. Canada was largely spared the impact of his “Liberation Day” tariffs in April 2025 by its pre-existing free trade deal with the US (and Mexico), but earlier this month, as expected, the US declined to extend that deal for another 16-year term. It’s now subject to annual renegotiations. Then, last week, the White House revealed tariffs as high as 50% on a selection of Canadian products including, for the first time, items previously protected by the trade agreement. The US called it retaliation for Canadian trade practices.

Meanwhile, It’s true that the US revealed tariffs against dozens more countries just days later, but there has been something odd about the lopsided attention paid to Canada, which most US presidents tend to politely ignore. Most of the tariffs Trump of late revealed were in the range of about 10%, but Canada was hit by 50% tariffs (albeit on a narrower range of exports). The president, it seems, wanted to send a message to Canada, but without hurting US consumers too much.

Notably, The tariffs also land differently here, given Trump’s shared desire to annex Canada as a 51st state. The president has ruled out using military force to accomplish that, saying instead that he would use “economic force” . Tariffs would meet that definition.

As per the latest buzz, There may have been little sign that the talk of annexation is anything more than typical Trumpian bluster, but even the suggestion, along with the tariffs, has been a shock for a Canadian political class that has long taken a friendly America as a law of nature – and has let Canada grow shockingly dependent on the US for defence and trade. An unfriendly, potentially even hostile US is a staggeringly consequential change. It’s hard to overestimate how huge a shock this has been.

In further updates, And it’s having a massive effect on our domestic politics, thus far to the benefit of the Liberal party and the prime minister, Mark Carney. The return of Trump to the White House upset an election last year that the Liberals had been set to lose decisively. Canada’s Conservatives were cruising to an easy win with a campaign focused on public safety and the cost of living, but once Trump began musing about annexation, the Liberals dumped Justin Trudeau, replaced him with Carney, wrapped themselves in the flag, and won decisively. Carney remains popular, largely because Canadians see him as the right choice to deal with Trump.

On top of that, US pressure is complicating Canada’s increasingly fraught internal politics in other ways. Canada does not have a true national economy, but a series of regional ones. Ontario and Quebec, the most populous provinces, are heavily dependent on manufacturing. In western Canada, particularly the provinces of Alberta and Saskatchewan, the economies depend more on exporting natural resources, including oil. Most of this goes to the US, as Canada lacks the transportation infrastructure to readily export it elsewhere (there’s that dependency).

The response has therefore been more fragmented than unified. Ontario has pursued a strategy of confrontation ; the western provinces have preferred to appeal to shared interests with the US. These are obvious fissures that the US could choose to exploit. It was strange to see, when the most recent round of tariffs was revealed, that most of the economic damage landed on Ontario and Quebec and the province of British Columbia – three jurisdictions that have taken stronger anti-Trump positions. The economies of Alberta and Saskatchewan were relatively spared.

title: Ayodhya Ki Ramlila to make its Delhi debut this year Ft. Ravi Kishan as Ram, Rakesh Bedi, and Vindu Dara Singh
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

After seven editions in Ayodhya, the star-studded Ayodhya Ki Ramlila is set to make its Delhi debut this year. The 11-day production will be staged at the Constitution Club of India from October 10 to 20, bringing its star cast to the Capital for the first time.

Adding to this, A glimpse of celebs who have performed in previous year’s Ayodhya Ki Ramlila ft. Manika Vishwakarma and Rahul Bucchar, Star Ravi Kishan as Ram, Rakesh Bedi, Puneet Issar, Manoj Tiwari and Vindu Dara Singh will feature this year Explaining the shift, organiser Subhash Malik says the Ramlila is being moved to Delhi because storms in Ayodhya during the Dussehra period often disrupt its live telecast.

Meanwhile, “This has been done due to logistical reasons,” he says, adding, “This Ramlila is known for its massive reach as it is telecast on national television as well as local cable and YouTube, with almost 62 crore rupees viewership across 50 countries. But to ensure that its regular followers in Ayodhya don’t remain deprived of viewing it, we aim to organise it in its second phase in Ayodhya from January 15; like how we did in 2024 when the Ayodhya Ram Mandir Pran Pratishtha ceremony was performed.”

Notably, The production, which began during the Covid-19 pandemic, will once again feature star and MP Ravi Kishan as Ram. “In the past, two Miss India Universe, namely Manika Vishwakarma (2025) and Rhea Singha (2024) have played the part of Sita in two different years. This year too, we are looking forward to roping in an equally popular name for the part,” adds Malik.

As per the latest buzz, Besides the central characters, Arun Bakshi will play Ravana, while Puneet Issar will portray Parashuram, Vindu Dara Singh will play Shiva, Raza Murad will essay Ahiravan and King Janak, Avtar Gill will appear as Narad Muni and Ved Sagar as Lakshman. Manoj Tiwari , Rakesh Bedi and Rahul Bucchar will also play key roles in select episodes. Malik adds, “Star Bhagyashree and singer Malini Awasthi, who have earlier enacted parts in this Ramlila, are also being approached again.”

In further updates, “I’m excited to perform in Delhi and then in Ayodhya in January,” says Vindu, adding, “My father (Dara Singh) used to play Hanumanji and Shivji. I have earlier played Hanumanji in Ramlila, and now I have been playing Shivji for the last few years and thoroughly enjoying it”

On top of that, Star Arun Bakshi, who plays Ravana in Ayodhya Ki Ramleela, says, “I am excited to play the role of Ravana as this is the world’s largest viewed Ramlila, and more so now that it will be performed in Delhi.” Singer Malini Awasthi, who played the role of Mata Shabri, shared that she is still figuring out about featuring this year as well.
Deep Saxena writes on Bollywood, OTT, television, food and culture for the daily Entertainment & Lifestyle supplement, HT City.

title: ‘Take a chill pill’: Cockroach Janta Party's Saurav Das tells Kangana Ranaut after she calls him simply useless

title: Eagles place EDGE Jonathan Greenard on PUP list prior to start of training camp
body: Here's what's trending across the USA right now:
The Philadelphia Eagles revealed on Wednesday morning that Jonathan Greenard will begin 2026 training camp on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list.
Adding to this, Greenard suffered a pectoral strain while lifting prior to camp.

Meanwhile, The PUP list is a tool teams use for players prior to the start of training camp, in case the player is not ready for the start of the regular season. The PUP list must be applied to a player prior to the start of training camp, or it cannot be used at all. Once a player practices in camp, at all, they immediately become ineligible for the PUP list during the regular season. The player cannot participate in practice while on the PUP list.

Notably, The benefit of the PUP list is that a player is eligible to come off of it during training camp, or, if the team deems it necessary, after the first four games of the regular season. Once the regular season starts and the player remains on the PUP list, they must spend the first four weeks on the PUP list, and they would not count toward one of the 53 roster spots. (They would still count toward one of the 90 roster spots while on PUP during training camp.)
As per the latest buzz, The Eagles traded a pair of third-round picks for Greenard during the draft. They also signed him to a four-year deal worth $98 million.
In further updates, Greenard was a Texans third-round pick in 2020. He will turn 29 years old in May.

title: Patrick Clancy continues testifying in his ex-wife’s murder trial. Follow live updates.
body: Here's what's trending across the USA right now:

After an emotional day of testimony on Monday, Patrick Clancy , the former husband of Lindsay Clancy and the father of the three children she is charged with killing in January 2023, returned to the stand on Wednesday.

Adding to this, Patrick Clancy testified about the days and weeks before the children were killed in their Duxbury home, and prosecutors began to ask him about the day they were found dead. On Wednesday, prosecutors continued that line of questioning. The 911 call he made after arriving home is expected to be played in court.

Meanwhile, While on the stand Monday, he also recounted the medications Lindsay Clancy was taking, her health and demeanor, and the “intrusive thoughts” she told him she was having about suicide and harming their children.

Notably, Patrick Clancy, 38, who has remarried and lives in New York, testified for more than two hours Monday , growing emotional at times when describing his children’s interests and personalities before they were killed.

As per the latest buzz, During opening statements earlier on Monday, prosecutors and Lindsay Clancy’s attorney presented opposing arguments about whether she was in psychosis on the day of the killings.
In further updates, Prosecutor Shanan Buckingham claimed Lindsay Clancy “was not a woman in the throes of psychosis,” but acted “intentionally, rationally, and swiftly.”

On top of that, Clancy’s attorney, Kevin Reddington, emphasized that the case is about “women’s health and postpartum psychosis,” pushing back on the state’s assertions about Clancy’s mental state. He shared that Plymouth District Attorney Timothy Cruz, in bringing murder charges, knew “it was going to kill the soul of this young woman.”

While she has admitted to strangling her children, Clancy has pleaded not guilty to the criminal charges, saying she was suffering from severe postpartum mental illness and heard a voice telling her to kill the children and herself. (Clancy survived the attempted suicide but remains paralyzed and in a wheelchair.)

title: YES Network, MSG Networks to exit Gotham app for DAZN streaming service
body: Here's what's trending across the USA right now:
The YES Network and MSG Networks will soon have a new streaming home.

Adding to this, The independently owned, top-tier regional sports networks that air local games for teams including MLB's New York Yankees and the NBA's New York Knicks are moving their direct-to-consumer streaming offerings to DAZN.

Meanwhile, Yankees followers will still be able to finish out the season on Gotham , and the migration will occur during the 2026-2027 NBA and NHL seasons. YES also airs the NBA's Brooklyn Nets, while MSG Networks has the rights to the NHL's New York Rangers, Islanders, Buffalo Sabres and New Jersey Devils.
Notably, Pay TV bundle customers who get access to each network through their cable provider will be able to stream those games on DAZN for free.
As per the latest buzz, Pricing details for the New York-area teams on DAZN haven't yet been rolled out. Various subscription plans for the Gotham sports app started at about $209.99 per year.

In further updates, The move to DAZN for some of the most popular professional teams comes as the regional sports network model faces severe pressure . Main Street Sports, the former owner of a portfolio of networks for MLB, NBA and NHL teams, shut down in the spring following a bankruptcy filing and various maneuvers that left the business often unable to make payments to teams for the rights to carry games.

On top of that, While YES and MSG have not been directly involved in that turmoil — MSG Networks is independently owned by Knicks and Rangers owner James Dolan, and YES, by a group including the Yankees — each channel has been affected by similar cord-cutting headwinds despite strong ratings.
DAZN has been among the suitors in a relatively strong position during the shakeout of streaming-only sports rights formerly owned by Main Street.
